item.title: Ten-Year Cycle in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Why Timing Changes the Reading
item.description: The ten-year cycle shows the main life theme of a decade. Read it after the birth chart and before the annual year.

item.title: The Four Transformations in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Fame, Power, Gain, and Friction
item.description: A plain-English guide to the four transformations: recognition, authority, gain, and friction. Read them by the life area where they appear.

item.title: Palace Context in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Why Location Comes First
item.description: In Zi Wei Dou Shu, a star changes meaning depending on where it lands. Learn the plain-English idea of palace context.

item.title: Triad and Opposite in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Read Four Areas Together
item.description: A plain-English guide to the Zi Wei Dou Shu triad and opposite method: read the main area together with money, career, and outside environment.

item.title: Body Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Where Life Pushes You Later
item.description: The Body Palace shows later-life focus: money, career, movement, relationship, or another area that becomes hard to ignore.

item.title: Parents Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Family Influence and Support
item.description: The Parents Palace shows early influence, elders, rules, protection, pressure, and the kind of support a person may receive.

item.title: Inner Life Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Mindset, Rest, and Endurance
item.description: Often called the Fortune or Mental Palace, this area shows inner reserves, emotional comfort, rest, and long-term endurance.

item.title: Property Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Home, Assets, and Stability
item.description: The Property Palace shows home, real estate, family base, long-term assets, and the sense of having a stable place.

item.title: Career Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Role, Responsibility, and Position
item.description: The Career Palace is about role and responsibility. Read it with the Wealth Palace to separate career position from income path.

item.title: Friends and Network Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu
item.description: This palace points to friends, helpers, teams, staff, audiences, and cooperation risks in a modern reading.

item.title: Outside Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Travel, Markets, and Platforms
item.description: The Outside Palace shows what happens beyond your familiar environment: travel, relocation, public exposure, clients, and larger platforms.

item.title: Health Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Pressure, Weak Points, and Care
item.description: The Health Palace should be read carefully as a pressure and self-care area, not as a replacement for medical advice.

item.title: Wealth Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: How Money Comes In
item.description: The Wealth Palace is about how money is made and handled. Read it with career, outside opportunities, and the person’s baseline.

item.title: Children Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Legacy, Output, and Responsibility
item.description: The Children Palace can be read as children, creative output, long-term responsibility, and what continues after you.

item.title: Spouse Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Relationship Style
item.description: The Spouse Palace helps read relationship style, partnership pressure, and how a person tends to meet or handle committed relationships.

item.title: Siblings Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Peers, Sharing, and Boundaries
item.description: The Siblings Palace is not only about brothers and sisters. It also points to peers, shared resources, and cooperation boundaries.

item.title: Life Palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu: What It Means
item.description: The Life Palace is the starting point of a Zi Wei Dou Shu chart. Learn how to read it without getting lost in technical star names.
